description: Document Issue #21 truthfully in the spec-driven artifacts and both READMEs. Update .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/{requirements,design,tasks}.md and README.md + README.ja.md to describe the share feature, the chosen OGP image approach and its honest tradeoff (SVG via Lambda, cached; some crawlers do not render SVG og:image), the crawler-readable /share HTML path (how a SPA still serves per-series meta tags and how a human is redirected into the app), the language-query permalink, the caching, and the new infra (two no-Bedrock Lambdas, /og + /share HTTP API routes, CloudFront behaviors). Map each of the three issue acceptance criteria.
steps: Update .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/requirements.md with a new requirement block for sharing/OGP (user story + acceptance criteria mirroring Issue #21's three criteria: OGP generation method decided+implemented; crawler-readable meta tags for the SPA; disclaimer included in shared content).

Update .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/design.md: describe the design decisions - OG image is generated as SVG by a Lambda (GET /og) and cached in DynamoDB keyed by seriesId+situation+lang; the honest tradeoff vs PNG (sharp native binaries are risky under esbuild/Lambda bundling, so SVG is chosen; some crawlers do not render an SVG og:image - document the raster path for a future PNG upgrade); the /share Lambda returns per-series OG/Twitter meta HTML with a redirect into the SPA (criterion 2); CloudFront routes /og and /share to the API; permalink+lang handling; and that neither new Lambda calls Bedrock.
Update .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/tasks.md marking the Issue #21 tasks and their status.

Update README.md: add a 'Share a series / prediction (permalinks + OGP)' section under the feature list and/or architecture, documenting the share button (Web Share + copy fallback), the ?lang= permalink, the /og SVG + /share HTML endpoints, the caching, the disclaimer in shared content, and the SVG-vs-PNG crawler caveat. Update the Architecture backend bullet (now FIVE Lambdas; routes now include GET /og and GET /share; CloudFront has extra behaviors) so the docs stay truthful.
Mirror the same additions in README.ja.md (Japanese), keeping it consistent with README.md.
Run `PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" npm run build && npm test && npm run synth` once more to confirm docs-only changes did not break anything.
Commit, e.g. `docs(issue-21): document share/OGP design, endpoints, caching, and SVG tradeoff in specs and both READMEs`.
acceptance_criteria: requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md describe the share/OGP feature and map Issue #21's three acceptance criteria.

README.md and README.ja.md both document the share button, ?lang= permalink, /og + /share endpoints, caching, disclaimer, and the SVG-vs-PNG crawler tradeoff, and the architecture bullets reflect FIVE Lambdas and the new routes/behaviors.
`npm run build`, `npm test`, and `npm run synth` still pass.
findings: A prior commit (FEAT-002, likely cbbd3ce/5125e8d) had already added Requirement 21 to requirements.md, an Issue #21 design section (shared builders, /og + /share Lambdas, DynamoDB cache, CloudFront routing), tasks.md E1/E2, and share/OGP sections in both READMEs with the FIVE-Lambdas + GET /og/GET /share wording. This feature VERIFIED those and filled the remaining gaps rather than duplicating: (1) requirements.md Requirement 21 - added the issue three-criteria mapping note plus criteria 5-6 for the frontend Share button (Web Share + clipboard copy + manual-copy fallback, feature-detected) and the ?lang= permalink precedence/persistence; (2) design.md - added a frontend ShareButton/permalink subsection and an honest SVG-vs-PNG tradeoff + future raster/PNG upgrade-path subsection; (3) tasks.md - added E3 (FEAT-003 share button + lang permalink + e2e) and E4 (this docs feature); (4) both READMEs - added the Share button + ?lang= permalink bullet and extended the SVG caveat with the PNG upgrade path. Verification green from repo root: npm run build, npm test (shared 62, backend 149, frontend 206, infra 13 - all pass), npm run synth.
